# 5-Day Lisbon Family Itinerary

A relaxed Lisbon plan for **2 adults + 1 child (age 9)**, built around **museums, easy walking, one beach day, and kid-friendly food**. Budget is kept within **€2,400 excluding flights**, with local transport and rainy-day backups included.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Plan

### Day 1: Baixa, Alfama, and the Riverfront
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and take an easy walk through **Baixa** to **Praça do Comércio** and the riverfront.
- **Afternoon:** Visit the **Lisbon Story Centre** or a light museum stop, then ride the **Santa Justa area** and wander the lower streets at a slow pace.
- **Evening:** Dinner in **Alfama** with simple options like grilled fish, chicken, soup, and rice; finish with a short miradouro stop if energy allows.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Swap the river walk for the **Lisbon Story Centre**, **MUDE** (design museum), and a café stop in Baixa.

**Estimated local transport:** **€12–€20**
- Airport transfer by taxi/ride-hail or metro + short rides
- 1–2 tram/metro trips for the day

### Day 2: Belém Museums and Riverside Icons
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Belém** for the **Jerónimos Monastery exterior**, **Pastéis de Belém**, and a gentle riverside stroll.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one museum: **MAAT** for modern architecture or the **Coach Museum** for a child-friendly indoor visit.
- **Evening:** Early dinner back in central Lisbon; keep it simple with piri-piri chicken, pasta, or seafood rice.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Focus on **Coach Museum + MAAT + café break** and skip the outdoor promenade.

**Estimated local transport:** **€10–€18**
- Tram/bus or taxi to Belém
- Return metro/taxi if the child is tired

### Day 3: Parque das Nações and Oceanário Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Visit the **Oceanário de Lisboa** early to avoid crowds.
- **Afternoon:** Walk the easy waterfront paths in **Parque das Nações**, ride the cable car if desired, and stop for ice cream or a snack.
- **Evening:** Dinner in the area or return to the center for a calmer meal.
- **Rainy-day backup:** The **Oceanário** already works well in bad weather; add the **Pavilion of Knowledge** if you want more indoor time.

**Estimated local transport:** **€14–€24**
- Metro to Oriente and back
- Optional cable car or short taxi ride

### Day 4: Beach Day in Cascais
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/sun.svg
- **Morning:** Take the train to **Cascais** and start with a beach walk at **Praia da Rainha** or a nearby sheltered cove.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3c/Beach_near_Lisbon_Portugal%2C_1994..jpg Alt=Morning:** Take the train to **Cascais** and start with a beach walk at **Praia da Rainha** or a nearby sheltered cove, Lisbon, Portugal
- **Afternoon:** Keep it light with sand time, a seaside lunch, and a slow stroll through the old town.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4c/Lisbon_%281600%29_detail_1.jpg Alt=Afternoon:** Keep it light with sand time, a seaside lunch, and a slow stroll through the old town, Lisbon, Portugal
- **Evening:** Return to Lisbon for an early dinner and an easy night.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Replace the beach with **Cascais town**, the **Marina**, and a relaxed indoor lunch; if the weather is very poor, stay in Lisbon and do **Gulbenkian Museum** instead.

**Estimated local transport:** **€18–€30**
- Round-trip train for 3
- Possible local taxi/walks in Cascais

### Day 5: Gulbenkian, Eduardo VII, and a Gentle Farewell
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **Morning:** Visit the **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** for an easy, high-quality culture stop.
- **Afternoon:** Walk through **Parque Eduardo VII** or relax with a long lunch and souvenir shopping in **Avenida da Liberdade**.
- **Evening:** Farewell dinner in a family-friendly restaurant with a final pastel de nata stop.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Spend more time at **Gulbenkian**, then use nearby cafés and indoor shopping on Avenida da Liberdade.

**Estimated local transport:** **€8–€16**
- Metro and short walk/taxi
- Minimal transit if staying central

## Family Cost Plan for Lisbon

| Category | Estimated cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Local transport | **€62–€108** | Metro, tram, taxis, and one Cascais day trip |
| Museums and attractions | **€140–€240** | Oceanário, Gulbenkian, one or two paid museum stops, optional cable car |
| Food and drinks | **€420–€700** | Mix of casual lunches, family dinners, snacks, and desserts |
| Beach day extras | **€30–€70** | Sunbeds/snacks/ice cream if needed |
| Buffer for extras | **€150–€250** | Taxis, treats, rain-day flexibility |
| **Estimated total** | **€802–€1,368** | Well within your **€2,400** budget, leaving room for nicer meals or a better hotel |
